name: PSNR-based Quality Estimation for Ray Casting
definition: A method to estimate sampling artifacts in Direct Volume Rendering (DVR) by treating rendered images as noisy signals. It uses Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) to quantify the dispersion of pixel colors across multiple renders with different stochastic jitter seeds, providing a numerical quality metric instead of subjective human evaluation.
summary: PSNR-based Quality Estimation for Ray Casting objectively quantifies sampling noise in volume rendering by measuring pixel color variance across multiple stochastic renders, distinguishing it from reference-based image compression metrics.
